title: Flatness of a module over a localization agrees over the base
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring, $W\subseteq A$ a multiplicative subset ($1\in W$, $vw\in W$ for $v,w\in W$) and $\lambda:A\to A'$ a homomorphism of commutative rings which is a localization of $A$ at $W$: (a) $\lambda(w)$ is a unit for every $w\in W$; (b) every element of $A'$ is $\lambda(a)\lambda(w)^{-1}$ with $a\in A$, $w\in W$; (c) $\lambda(a)=0$ implies $wa=0$ for some $w\in W$ (for instance $A'=W^{-1}A$ with $a\mapsto a/1$). Let $M$ be an $A'$-module, regarded as an $A$-module via $\lambda$. Then $M$ is a flat $A'$-module if and only if $M$ is a flat $A$-module [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]. In particular, if $\psi:A'\to C$ is a ring map such that $\psi\circ\lambda:A\to C$ is flat, then $\psi$ is flat.
